name: Pragma Systems Adaptive Base Layer
description:
A long-sleeve fitted base layer from Pragma Systems, the augmentation-adjacent apparel division of a larger biotech corponation. The shirt itself looks unremarkable — a matte charcoal or off-white compression top with flat seams and a crew neck — but the fabric is woven with a distributed thermal-regulation mesh that responds to body temperature, venting when core temperature rises and tightening insulation when it drops. The response is passive and requires no power source; it's a material property, not an electronic system.

The real selling point for the augmented community is the construction: the shoulder and upper arm panels are reinforced with micro-articulated seams that flex and recover around subdermal chrome, and the fabric at the wrist can be cut and heat-sealed without fraying, allowing custom openings for hardwired ports or sensor arrays. It's marketed to 'active professionals' but the aug-community forums have made it their own.
functionality: Passive thermal regulation via material properties (no power required). Aug-compatible construction with micro-articulated shoulder seams and heat-sealable wrist openings for hardwired port access.
what_it_says: You're augmented, you're practical, and you've done your research — or you have a job that demands both performance and comfort.
story_hooks: A batch of Pragma base layers was distributed to a corporate security team before a major operation. One of those layers has ended up in a Tier 2 second-hand store, and the serial number traces back to someone who's officially listed as alive.

The thermal-regulation weave in recent batches has an undocumented secondary property: it holds a faint thermal impression of the wearer's body heat pattern for several hours after removal, visible to the right sensors.
Pragma is beta-testing a version with embedded biometric monitoring. The beta batch looks identical to the retail version. Some units have already shipped without the testers knowing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, understated compression top that reads as minimalist corporate wear at first glance. The matte finish and clean lines create an almost clinical aesthetic—precisely engineered rather than fashionable. On an augmented wearer, small irregularities in the shoulder and upper arm seams become visible: micro-articulations that follow the geometry of subdermal chrome like a second skin.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit through the torso and sleeves; snug but not restrictive. Follows the body's contours closely enough to accommodate bulky augmentations without bunching. The fabric hugs muscular or cybernetic arms equally well.
physical_description.primary_material: Synthetic blend with woven thermal-regulation mesh; the mesh is passive—no power requirement. Matte finish suggests treated microfiber or advanced polyamide composite.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and almost rubber-like to the touch, with subtle ribbed texture where thermal mesh is densest. Flat-lock seams create zero friction points. Wrist edges designed for clean heat-sealing and minimal fraying.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey or off-white, deliberately neutral. No branding visible on the front; optional discrete Pragma Systems logo on inner collar or shoulder blade.
physical_description.closures: Crew neck, no closures required. Designed to layer under or wear as standalone. Wrists are open-ended for customization.
distinctive_features: Micro-articulated shoulder and upper arm seams that flex around subdermal augmentations
Passive thermal-regulation mesh woven throughout fabric
Heat-sealable wrist panels for custom port openings or sensor array integration
Flat seams throughout to avoid pressure points over implants
Reinforced panels on shoulders sized to accommodate chrome cyberlimbs
Unmarked construction—no visible branding except interior label
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 boundary. Pragma Systems positions it as Tier 2 'active professional' wear, but street price and aug-community adoption place it functionally Tier 3.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals augmentation-friendly practicality. Worn by corpo augmentation consultants, street med-techs, underground surgeons, and any embodied professional who's too smart to ignore their chrome's physical needs. The lack of branding appeals to those who want function without visible corporate loyalty.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn pristine by recent purchasers; develops minor wear patterns at wrist edges and shoulder seams with use. Heat-sealed custom openings create intentional irregularities that look deliberate rather than damaged.
